page: Amazon Web Services c8in.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated 3.9 GHz Intel x86_64 processor delivering 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 2 threads per core. The configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, matching a compute-tailored 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB per vCPU. Discrete hardware accelerators and GPUs are not included.

The instance delivers a high baseline network throughput of 50 Gbps, accommodating high-volume network ingress and egress. It contains no bundled local disk storage, necessitating the use of Amazon Elastic Block Store or external network filesystems. This decouples compute processing from persistent storage, directing high-throughput network paths toward remote storage arrays and cluster interconnects.

With its combination of high clock speed processing and dense network bandwidth, the instance delivers high compute efficiency per core without the cost overhead of local NVMe arrays. Tradeoffs include reliance on external storage for disk operations. Workload fit includes network-heavy compute jobs, distributed cluster workers, CI/CD build pipelines, ETL tasks, and high-traffic web serving tiers.
